title: Life Manager Cloud: A Manager That Reports Only What It Has Verified

# Life Manager Cloud: A Manager That Reports Only What It Has Verified

Most AI assistants promise results. Life Manager Cloud is built the other way around: it reports a listing or an earning only after it has been verified, and it says plainly what it does not promise.

Life Manager is being built as one proactive manager for work, money, everyday responsibilities, body, and mind. It chooses useful priorities, carries work forward, and verifies outcomes, without a daily prompt. That last part — verifies outcomes — is the part that matters most when money is involved.

## The difference is verification, not promises

A promise is cheap. A verified result is not. When money is involved, the difference between "the manager tried something" and "the manager earned something verified" is the whole product. Life Manager keeps that distinction visible: attempted actions are distinguished from verified payments, and only the verified side is reported as a result.

## What "verified before it is reported" means here

The first Cloud earning workflow is being connected to Capafy. Capafy requires Publisher Certification and publisher confirmation of selected Skills and configuration before each Agent version can go live. Life Manager reports listings and earnings only after Capafy confirms them. Attempted actions are distinguished from verified payments. That distinction is stated on the product page, not added here.

## What this manager does not promise

Earnings are not guaranteed. The complete Cloud-to-Capafy path is still being verified. Some capabilities require setup or are still being developed, and the README and code are public on GitHub so what is implemented can be checked. A manager that says this plainly is easier to trust than one that promises income it cannot verify.

## Not a chatbot that waits for instructions

No daily instructions or user-defined goals and budgets are required by the product design. The manager chooses work and priorities. Provider-specific identity verification, account connections, and interviews may still require your involvement — that limit is also stated on the page. Calendar travel-time planning is one workflow inside this manager, not the product itself.

## The same manager, two ways to run it

Run the same open-source core on your own computer, or use Life Manager Cloud, hosted on a dedicated Maritime VM and used from your phone. Maritime is where it is hosted, not a separate product or edition. The manager, the pricing, and the way it works are the same.

## Pricing, stated plainly

Life Manager Cloud is $29/month after a 7-day free trial. Billing is set up in the web app after Calendar setup; no payment details are required at signup. Price on the site: 29 USD. There is one plan on the site, not a tier list.

## How it starts

Start with Google identity only. Google sign-in verifies identity only. Signup does not require Calendar or Gmail inbox access, a task prompt, goals, budget, or payout details. Progress and verified results are designed to go to your sign-in email.

## Try the manager, not the promise

If the idea of a manager that reports only verified results sounds useful, start from the product page, where the price, the trial, and the sign-up requirements are stated plainly:

- Life Manager: https://aniccaai.com/lm

One manager. Verified results, one step at a time.
